- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; check for lagged sentiment influence and adjust forecast mid-series.  
- Model often overreacts to recent highs/lows; apply smoothing: if forecast deviates >2% from 10-day moving average, adjust toward it.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in bearish sentiment cycles; add 1–2% buffer if sentiment <0.33 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day trend.
